text:
maria: sec-scan-bot opened an alert: 3 CVEs hit inference runtime deps (protobuf, FlashAttention kernel, Triton plugin). Can we triage and set patch priority?
sec-bot: [AUTO] vuln: PROTOBUF-2026-001 (high), FLASHATTN-2026-002 (critical), TRITON-2026-003 (high). links: https://sec.example/cves/PROTOBUF-2026-001
liam: can you paste the quick impact notes? remote exploit vs local?
arjun: protobuf looks like a parsing bug that can be triggered by crafted model metadata (remote if model uploads are allowed). CVSS 7.8. exploit proof-of-concept exists on private repo.
maria: FlashAttention kernel vuln allows out-of-bounds reads in certain fused kernels compiled for A100 with flash kernels. vendor patch out today but requires rebuilding kernel artifacts. exploit maturity = medium, but can leak kv-cache.
jen: Triton plugin issue is a use-after-free in custom backend handler, only when using our Triton custom op (we ship a small wrapper). CVSS 7.5.
paul: summary: all 3 affect inference hosts. protobuf & Triton are user-space libs we can hot-restart; FlashAttention kernel touches compiled CUDA kernels and may need full process restart and re-deploy of compiled wheels.
liam: priority suggestion? protobuf = P0 for public model uploads, Triton = P1, FlashAttn = P1 but fast follow with canary.
arjun: agree. If customers can upload models (hosted api), protobuf must be patched ASAP. For Dedicated/private where model uploads are disabled, lower immediate urgency but still scheduled.
maria: mitigation for protobuf: block model uploads at edge AND disable multipart POSTs as temporary filter. Ops can put WAF rule.
ops-sre: I can add a temporary rule to drop Content-Type: multipart/form-data for /v1/models/upload on hosted region us-east1. ETA ~20m.
jen: for Triton and FlashAttn we should do canary rollout on Dedicated pools first (1 node), then 10% of hosted, monitor OOMs and latency. plan to keep old binary as fallback.
paul: I'll own Triton plugin patch + CI build. I need a short checklist: build, smoke test, canary deploy, monitor, full deploy, rollback plan.
paul: checklist (paste)
```
- bump triton-plugin -> v2.3.1-patch
- run unit+integration on x86/gpu images
- build wheel and docker image
- deploy canary to pool:d-patch-canary-1
- monitor 1h (latency, errors, mem)
- promote if green, else rollback
```
arjun: protobuf patch plan: bump to protobuf 3.21.12 (or vendor backport if needed). verify model upload parsing in staging with fuzz corpus.
jen: FlashAttention note: vendor provides new wheels with ABI change. That will break older cached kv files. Need to invalidate prefix cache for legacy deployments or support dual-path loader.
maria: cache invalidation strategy? we can't evict all kv caches live. Suggest rolling restart of inference pods while toggling kv-prefix-version header so clients regen.
liam: also verify KMS usage: model keys are decrypted by runtime service. If exploit can read KV memory, could it leak model encryption keys if those live in process. We must ensure keys are not persisted in plaintext and decrypted per-request with short-lived in-memory only and zeroed after use.
jen: KMS integration question: does Triton process have direct access to KMS? currently decryption is performed by model-loader service which has KMS IAM. Triton runs as same pod with unix socket. Risk surface is loader memory exposure.
arjun: mitigation: rotate keys used for models, add strict IAM binding so only model-loader SA can decrypt, and add KMS audit log pipeline alerting on decrypt ops from unusual identities.
maria: ops-sre, can we add an IAM binding and a Splunk alert for kms.decrypt spikes? Also restrict decrypt rights to group inference-loaders only.
ops-sre: yes. proposed gcloud command (example):
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/r-infr/locations/global/keyRings/models/cryptoKeys/model-key \
  --member=serviceAccount:model-loader@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
ops-sre: will also add an alert: when cloudkms.decrypt count > 5/min across unexpected SA -> create PagerDuty.
paul: RBAC change request: create group `inference-loaders` and map to model-loader SA only. I can make infra PR.
liam: audit logging: we need decrypted key usage logged to long-term audit store and tied to request id. Add a header X-Request-Id into decrypt calls.
jen: AND ensure audit logs are forwarded to compliance retention (7 years) and immutability flag set.
maria: operational decisions:
- protobuf patching is P0 for hosted model uploads. schedule immediate patch and hot-restart. -> assign arjun (RINF-3217)
- Triton plugin patch P1, canary first -> assign paul (RINF-3218)
- FlashAttention wheels P1, but requires coordinated may-break cached kv -> schedule with devex & release notes -> assign jen (RINF-3219)
- KMS/RBAC/audit follow-up -> ops-sre + liam (RINF-3220)
liam: timelines? arjun ETA fix + PR in 2 hours, deploy to staging by EOD, hosted patch tonight if green.
arjun: yes. fuzzing run now, I'll ping when PR is up.
paul: I'll start Triton build now, may need 30-60m for CI GPU runs.
ops-sre: WAF rule applied for uploads in us-east1 (id: waf-1769-01). Monitoring in Grafana dashboard `vuln-triage/PROTOBUF`.
maria: create an incident/triage channel and link to Jira tickets. I'll open #inc-176912-proto-triage and add participants.
jen: add customer-facing comms template for Dedicated/private customers noting scheduled restarts and compat notes.
maria: thanks all. Please update tickets and ping here when PRs are green. :+1:
